questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to be able to select relevant courses. It was also important to choose a place where I could practice my sport while studying and enjoying a different culture than in Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a fantastic experience and it was the right choice to do it and totally worth the time spend on the practical things before going on exchange. I will fully recommend going on exchange at Griffith University, Gold Coast, Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I got some emails about orientation week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation week. Questions about courses and classes could be ask at the student center at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Getting courses approved before the start of the trimester could be difficult, but there was assistance at the student center and they informed me, that some of the courses start a week later, so no need to stress.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in the Griffith University Village.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in a 5-people apartment with a kitchen. The kitchen was not as clean as I would prefer, but it was functional.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It was an easy way to get housing before arrival and close to campus. It was nice with an opportunity to meet people with different backgrounds and socialize. I meet my friends here. 
The apartments were not that nice and not clean when I arrived, but the rooms were fine. When I was living in the village, there was a lot of construction work, which could make noise and was not nice to look at and took up a lot of space. So just be aware of that, before choosing to live in the Griffith University Village. Furthermore, it was an expensive rent.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I made my registration for courses on their internal website. It was easy to find and easy to use. However the approval of courses took quite a long time and I got my approvals late.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could get help by emailing them or by going to the student center.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got half of my applied courses approved. I managed to find other relevant courses instead of the ones I applied for in the beginning.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is an easy process, but be patient for the approval of courses. Otherwise go and ask for help at the student center. Have some extra courses ready to apply for.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level on the courses to be easier than in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
My lectures were only online which could be both good and bad. It was flexible, but also more boring to watch the lectures alone.
I had a couple of labs or workshops at campus during the week, but not many hours spend on campus, except for when I choose to go to the the library and study.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Exercise sports nutrition, Motor learning and control, Physiology of exercise, Research methods and statistics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The labs were good in Physiology of exercise.

questions.answer: Transportation to trips, flights and housing on holiday trips

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegetables were more expensive. Food, restaurants, and housing were similar to prices in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of clubs, both cultural, social and athletics.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would totally recommend to attend the orientation week. This is a great opportunity to meet new friends and get around campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I recommend going to the beaches, taking surf lessons, going to the national parks and take your swimming clothes with you, having a barbecue near the beach, doing snorkling, going on an island, having a dinner night with your friends, participate in a park run.
In generel I recommend to rent a car to get around.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was super easy. People are so kind in Australia.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend orientation week, be part of a club or do a voluntary job at campus to get to know more people. Don't be afraid to talk to people in your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness and the happy and calm ambience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be nervous, people are very friendly and you will easily find friends if you are attending the o-week or other socializing offers.
Enjoy it, don't be stressed, and try to adapt to the calming ambiance in Gold Coast. The workload is not as big as in Denmark.
Go to the beaches and see the nature and animal life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Enjoying my life with a lot of nice people in a more calm and beautiful environment, while studying.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing very challenging beside from being far away from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
